title: Adaptive Prometheus + OTel ingestion for inference KPI collection and SLO alignment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a resilient, low-cardinality metrics ingestion pipeline that captures Redwood-specific inference KPIs (token latency percentiles, per-request token counts, KV cache hit rates, batch sizes, model fallbacks) using OpenTelemetry for instrumentation and Prometheus-compatible storage for alerting and dashboards.

Background: Our serving runtime emits high-cardinality labels (user_route_id, full_prompt_hash, ephemeral_request_id) that currently flood Prometheus and blow up TSDB cardinality during integration tests. We also need tighter linkage between traces and metrics (exemplars) so runbook playbooks can jump from an SLO breach to a request trace quickly. The pipeline must support hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with the same instrumentation surface.

Scope:
- OTel Collector topology for ingesting metrics and traces from runtime pods and sidecars.
- Prometheus remote_write configuration (Cortex/Thanos) with relabeling and metric transformations implemented in the collector and at the remote_write ingress.
- Recording rules & aggregation for inference KPIs: p50/p95/p99 token latency, request_per_second, tokens_per_request, error_rate_by_model, kv_cache_hit_rate, tail_latency_by_batch_size.
- Cardinality control: label whitelisting, label value bucketing for model_variant and route, dropping ephemeral labels, and histogramless summaries for heavy cardinality dimensions.
- Exemplars: propagate trace IDs into metric exemplars so Grafana panels link to traces.
- Export contract for Private deployments: a small config bundle and validation script that lets customers run the same collector/recording rules in their VPC.

Trade-offs considered:
- Push vs pull: We standardize on OTel push (collectors) for private customers and kube-scrape for Prometheus in hosted mode; the collector will support both patterns.
- Where to do relabeling: Do expensive cardinality reduction in the OTel Collector so the remote storage gets bounded cardinality. This increases CPU on collectors but saves TSDB costs.
- Histogram vs summary: Use histograms with fixed buckets for latency and then recording rules to convert to percentiles. This avoids uncontrolled label explosion from summaries.

Non-goals: Full log pipeline work (separate ticket), and deep tracing sampling policy tuning (follow-on).
acceptance_criteria: OTel Collector Helm chart updated with new metric_pipeline, relabeling, and exemplar support merged to infra-telemetry repo (PR #974)
Recording rules implemented in telemetry-rules with tests and deployed to staging cluster: inference_latency_p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_request_avg, error_rate_per_model
Grafana dashboard 'Inference KPIs (Prometheus/OTel)' created and linked in docs with panels for p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution, and model_fallback_rate
Alerting rules added: inference_tail_latency_slo_breach (p99 > SLO), model_error_rate_spike (5m error_rate > 5%), and cardinality_watch (detected label cardinality increase > 10% over baseline)
Load test (k6) run with 100k synthetic requests across 50 model variants showing no >5x increase in unique TSDB series after relabeling rules applied
Exemplar linking verified: at least 95% of metric-based alert incidents include a trace exemplar URL in Grafana panels
Private deployment config bundle validated by solutions-engineering on a customer-like VPC and included in the private-deploy docs
tasks: Instrument runtime to expose prometheus metrics endpoint with standardized labels (model, model_variant, deployment, region, route_bucket)
Add exemplar propagation in runtime: attach trace_id as exemplar to latency histograms and request counters
OTel Collector config: receivers (prometheus, otlp), processors (batch, attributes, resource), exporters (remote_write, otlp), and metric_transformations to drop ephemeral labels
Write relabeling rules to bucket route -> route_bucket (hash -> low-cardinality mapping) and model_variant -> stable buckets
Create recording rules for all inference KPIs and add unit tests for each rule
Author Grafana dashboards and attach links to runbooks and playbooks
Add CI check: validate that new metrics do not exceed cardinality budget using a smoke script
Document private-deploy validation steps and pack the config bundle + validation script
notes: Related RFCs: RFC-58 (exemplar design), RFC-62 (label bucketing semantics)
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra-telemetry, and SRE. Agreed to prototype exemplar propagation and relabeling in a staging cluster.
2026-02-20: Prototype collector config committed. Verified prometheus receiver can scrape runtime metrics and OTel exporter remote_write works to staging Cortex.
2026-02-26: Discovered high cardinality from route_id and full_prompt_hash. Implemented attributes processor to drop full_prompt_hash and map route_id to route_bucket using hashing config.
2026-03-01: PR 974 opened for collector Helm chart changes. Security review requested for exporter endpoints (private deploy must use customer KMS for creds).

2026-03-05: Load test run. Initial numbers: raw series increased 12x without relabeling; after relabeling rules applied it dropped to 1.3x baseline. Added an extra relabel rule to collapse ephemeral_user_id.
2026-03-09: SRE feedback: recording rules must include per-region aggregation to avoid cross-region cardinality. Updated rules accordingly.

2026-03-12: Merged telemetry-rules for p50/p95/p99. Dashboard in review with PM and design. Next: finalize private bundle validation and merge infra-telemetry PR post security signoff. Blocker: need customer deployment template for VPC seat (blocked by solutions-engineering availability).
